title: Additive Number
summary: An additive number is a string of digits that can form an additive sequence with at least three numbers.
statement: An additive number is a string of digits that can form an additive sequence with at least three numbers. Each number after the first two must be the sum of the two preceding numbers. The sequence cannot include numbers with leading zeros. Return true if the string forms an additive number, otherwise return false.
constraints: Return whether all digits can be split into at least three integers where every integer after the first two equals their sum. No multi-digit integer may start with zero.
hints: Once the first two numbers are chosen, every later number is forced.
Enumerate the two initial split points, rejecting a multi-digit part that begins with zero.
Repeatedly form str(first+second) and require it at the current index, then shift the pair forward.
Accept only when the forced sequence consumes every digit; matching a prefix is not sufficient.
editorial: Every valid sequence is uniquely determined by its first two boundaries. For each legal pair, generate the decimal text of the required sum and match it at the next position. A mismatch ends that pair; consuming the whole string proves a sequence of at least three terms because both initial boundaries leave a suffix. The independent oracle uses separately structured split loops and the same arithmetic definition on 500 seeded strings.

tests.explanation: The complete split 1,1,2,3,5,8 is additive because each term is the sum of the preceding two.
The tempting split 1,02,3 is forbidden by the leading zero, and no other complete additive split exists.
